evidence: the-checks-are-installed: manifests/sysmon_base.pp:22-29 declare nagios-puppet.sh root:root 0755 from the module's file; the probe's first stat line expects root:root 755, and the content is rightly not hashed against the baseline because local change #4 (rules/local_changes.md) edits that file, while the other scripts are compared by their baseline sha256

the-elastic-check-is-unknown-without-elasticsearch: elastic_query_check.py (whole file) posts to http://localhost:9200/_search and on any exception prints PRINT_UNKOWN ('Unknown') then the exception and exits EXIT_UNKOWN (3); with nothing on 9200 urllib raises '<urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>', exactly what the probe expects (rc=3)

the-connection-checks-count-real-connections: check_netstat_conns.sh (whole file) counts netstat -an tcp LISTEN and ESTABLISHED lines into tcp_listen=/tcp_established= perfdata; sshd listening and the runner's SSH session make both non-zero, and check_netstat_cip.sh 22 counts the non-loopback remote IPs on :22 (num_of_ips); the third line asserts netstat exists (net-tools, local change #3)

purpose covered: Purpose matches the manifest (13 file resources installing node-side Nagios plugins; the header's 'zimbra' has no code, and the computed $packagename is unused). The outcomes table maps every resource. My run ALL_PASS, 22 checks: each script is executed as a monitoring server would and its status line and exit code checked, including the alarm paths: Puppet check OK / UNKNOWN under the run lock / CRITICAL when disabled / CRITICAL on a failed resource (agent exit 4 or 6); reboot OK and WARNING; package count OK, WARNING, stale-list alarm; bandwidth OK, WARNING, and CRITICAL with traffic from the ubuntu2 peer; latency OK and CRITICAL; CPU OK and CRITICAL under load; memory OK and CRITICAL; TLS cert OK and WARNING against a real local TLS server; Elasticsearch Unknown, OK, Critical with ordered events, and the request path/query recorded by a stand-in. File-handle, OS and netstat scripts have no alarm branch in the baseline, so OK with real counts is their full behaviour. Not exercised: some intermediate WARNING branches (memory, CPU, latency) and the cert CRITICAL, which are the same comparison code as the tested branches. The RedHat package-count branch and RedHat install are honestly uncovered, lifted_by rhel9. Mutating checks declare their changes (agent runs, locks, chattr, stand-in servers, peer pings) and are judged on read-only effects.
